title: Khaya senegalensis stochastic growth: harvested vs unharvested (annual pooled matrices)
question: Using COMPADRE's annual pooled matrices (2004-05, 2005-06), is stochastic lambda lower in high-harvest than unmanipulated populations, matching the direction reported by Gaoue & Ticktin?
hypothesis: lambda_s(high harvest) < lambda_s(unmanipulated); only 2 annual matrices per arm so uncertainty is large.
finding: Stochastic lambda high-harvest 0.9725 vs unmanipulated 0.9724 (difference +0.0001): the published harvest penalty is NOT reproduced from COMPADRE's two pooled annual matrices per arm; the paper's stochastic analysis used a different (ecoregion-specific, multi-year) structure.

result.paper_reported: stochastic lambda lower under high harvest in both ecoregions (dossier: 0.9913 vs 1.0345 moist; 0.9659 vs 0.9999 dry)
